_doc.purpose: Single source of truth for the strict source-line gate enforced by scripts/ci/check-source-lines.py. JSON cannot carry comments, so all policy commentary lives here under _doc.
_doc.enforcement: Full-tree, strict, no grandfathering: every PR to main is judged against the ENTIRE HEAD Git tree. Historical grandfathering (base/fork-point blob identity), the legacy ratchet, and the per-path allowlist mechanism (scripts/ci/source-line-allowlist.txt, deleted) no longer exist. Any maintained source file above its category limit fails, regardless of whether the same blob existed at the base commit, a fork point, or an earlier commit. The gate fails closed: a missing policy file, malformed JSON, an invalid limits table, or missing git history aborts with exit 2 instead of passing.

limits.production: Maintained first-party code and executable infrastructure (Java backend, Keycloak providers, Android Kotlin, frontend source, shell/python deploy and CI tooling, OpenTofu, workflow YAML). Physical-line budget per file: 500.
limits.test: Maintained first-party test code (paths containing a test directory segment, test-named files, browser test scripts, CI test scripts). Physical-line budget per file: 1500.

categories.generated: Machine-generated first-party artifacts that are never hand-edited: TypeScript declarations emitted from types, generated API transport clients, vendored third-party C sources inside the Android NDK bridge, lockfiles, Terraform lock files. Excluded from both budgets. This list is exact-path/pattern scoped and must stay small; do NOT route maintained code through it.
categories.vendored: Third-party code copied into the tree and never modified locally. Excluded from both budgets. Currently empty: the xdelta3 C sources are covered by the generated category entry (android/app/src/main/cpp/xdelta3/). Any new vendored dependency must be added here explicitly with PR justification, never inferred.
categories.immutable-history: Applied database migrations. java/**/src/main/resources/db/migration/V[0-9]*__*.sql is classified structurally by path convention, not per file: Flyway checksums make applied migrations immutable, and rewriting them would corrupt every deployed environment, so they are excluded from the 500-line production budget. A migration file becomes immutable the moment it is committed to this path; there is no per-file opt-in or opt-out. Maintained code living under a path that merely LOOKS like this convention (e.g. db/migrations/, or non-SQL sources placed under the real migration directory) is NOT covered and stays inside the production budget.

_doc.rationale_flyway: The Flyway exclusion is deliberately path-convention based so classification is objective and reviewable in the diff alone: either the file sits under java/**/src/main/resources/db/migration/V[0-9]*__*.sql or it does not. Per-file exceptions are the failure mode this gate exists to prevent, so none are supported anywhere in the policy.
